title: Workplace Disputes Very Common in UK Companies
paragraphs: Workplace disputes — serious disagreements between employees and their colleagues or with their employers — can take many forms.
Disagreements can arise over things like communication styles, how employees are treated, how workloads are shared, or over how much time an employee is absent from work.
And when disputes do arise, they can cost companies a lot in both time and money.
Now, a new survey has found that 93% of UK employers have experienced at least one workplace dispute in the last two years, with 63% resulting in attempted legal action.

Insurance firm Gallagher surveyed over 500 UK employers in September this year. It found that, on average, workplace disputes cost employers more than $3,400 to resolve, and 59% of employers said that dealing with disputes had taken up at least 25 hours of company time over the past two years.
And disputes can also affect a company's reputation.

Sixty-eight percent of employers said that the company's reputation had been affected by a dispute. This included 26% who experienced negative social media comments, 26% who were affected by negative online reviews and 24% who experienced further complaints from employees.

Employers also shared what types of disputes are increasing. Forty percent said that there was an increase in disagreements over flexible working, 37% said there was an increase in disputes over bullying, harassment or discrimination, and 36% said there was an increase in sickness, absence or disability-related disputes.

And as for the reasons for the increases, thirty-three percent of employers said that disputes were becoming more common because of the changing expectations of employees, while 30% said it was because of hybrid or remote working.

Alistair Dornan, a managing director at Gallagher, said that to avoid workplace disagreements becoming costly and time-consuming disputes, employers needed clear policies, manager training, and early intervention.

"Investing in manager training is key to this, ensuring those on the frontline have the confidence and skills to navigate difficult conversations, resolve issues early and prevent disputes becoming costly legal battles," said Dornan.
